title: Read This If You Wear Dentures 👆
body:
I've been stopped 4 times at dentist appointments this year.

Not because something was wrong.

Because people kept asking what happened to my mouth.

The first time was in January.

Routine cleaning. Same office I'd been going to for almost 8 years.

Same hygienist.
Same dentist.

Same speech I usually got:
"A little more inflammation." "Your gums are irritated again." "Maybe try a different gum brush."

Same story. Every visit.

I'm 67.
Retired school teacher.
Fixed income. Social security. Clipping coupons.

I lost my teeth younger than I should have.

Back then you didn't go to the dentist unless something was already falling apart.

Grown up poor. Coffee and cigarettes for breakfast. Soda and candy while young. No one taught us any better.

By 58, I had full dentures.

And by 60, I was spending half my life trying to make them work.

Polident. Efferdent. Baking soda. Dawn dish soap.

I love my dentures. They fit great. They look great. I haven't stopped smiling since I got them seven years ago.

But I never imagined something I wore every single day would almost kill me.

A little cough in the morning. Some sneezing I'd never had before. A scratchy throat at night that wouldn't go away.

body:
I've been stopped 4 times at dentist appointments this year.

Not because something was wrong.

Because people kept asking what happened to my mouth.

The first time was in January.

Routine cleaning. Same office I'd been going to for almost 8 years.

Same hygienist.
Same dentist.

Same speech I usually got:
"A little more inflammation." "Your gums are irritated again." "Maybe try a different gum brush."

Same story. Every visit.

I'm 67.
Retired school teacher.
Fixed income. Social security. Clipping coupons.

I lost my teeth younger than I should have.

Back then you didn't go to the dentist unless something was already falling apart.

Grown up poor. Coffee and cigarettes for breakfast. Soda and candy while young. No one taught us any better.

By 58, I had full dentures.

And by 60, I was spending half my life trying to make them work.

Polident. Efferdent. Baking soda. Dawn dish soap.

title: The hospital rule nobody tells denture wearers
body:

It's there because of pneumonia, and nobody told me about it until I was 70.

I had my hip replaced last fall. Four nights in the hospital.

title: Were Washington’s dentures really made out of wood?
body:
For 31 years I taught kids that George Washington had wooden teeth. I was wrong.

I only found out the truth after my stroke, and I wish I'd known it ten years sooner.

Here's what I didn't know.

By the day Washington became president, he had one tooth of his own left.

His false teeth were made of hippo ivory, cow and horse teeth, human teeth, gold wire and brass screws.

There wasn't a splinter of wood in any of them.

body:
I've been stopped 4 times at dentist appointments this year.

Not because something was wrong.

Because people kept asking what happened to my mouth.

The first time was in January.

Routine cleaning. Same office I'd been going to for almost 8 years.

Same hygienist.
Same dentist.

Same speech I usually got:
"A little more inflammation." "Your gums are irritated again." "Maybe try a different gum brush."

Same story. Every visit.

I'm 67.
Retired school teacher.
Fixed income. Social security. Clipping coupons.

I lost my teeth younger than I should have.

Back then you didn't go to the dentist unless something was already falling apart.

Grown up poor. Coffee and cigarettes for breakfast. Soda and candy while young. No one taught us any better.

By 58, I had full dentures.

And by 60, I was spending half my life trying to make them work.

Polident. Efferdent. Baking soda. Dawn dish soap.

body:
I want to tell you how much money I spent  denture adhesive that don't work before I found the right product.

My name is Anne. I am 68. For 8 years I went to the same CVS every 2 and a half weeks and bought the same tube of Fixodent. Same pink tube. Same price. Same result. title: The night I finally understood why my denture just wouldn’t stay put when I was eating.
body:
Have you ever caught yourself secretly avoiding your favorite foods because you don’t trust your denture to survive the very first bite?

I have. For years.

I told myself I was just being “careful,” that at my age you simply have to make a few compromises.
But the truth was much more uncomfortable.
I had stopped eating the things I loved. I treated my plate like a bomb technician treats a device that might explode.

Only soft foods. Tiny bites. Chew on the left, never the right. Don’t laugh while chewing. And always keep a napkin nearby—“just in case.”

The moment I finally reached my limit didn’t happen in a fancy restaurant.
It happened on an ordinary Sunday lunch at my daughter’s house.

Nothing special: roast, potatoes, vegetables, the usual chatter of grandchildren around the table.

My seven-year-old grandson Jamie held out the bowl and asked, “Grandma, do you want another piece?”
